name: GPT-6.2 Sol
description: GPT-6.2 Sol is OpenAI's efficient, versatile GPT-6.2 model for everyday work, from coding and writing to powering agents at scale. The API model id is gpt-6.2-sol. It accepts text and image input with text output, supports low, medium, high, xhigh, and max reasoning effort (but not none), and provides a 1,050,000-token context window (922,000 max input) with up to 128,000 output tokens. Responses API tools include web and file search, image generation, code interpreter, hosted shell, apply patch, skills, computer use, MCP, and tool search; it also supports streaming, function calling, structured outputs, and multi-agent delegation (beta). Standard per-million-token pricing is $2 input, $0.10 cached input, $2.50 cache writes (30-minute retention), and $10 output, unchanged from GPT-6.1 Sol. Prompts above 272K input tokens cost 2x input/cache and 1.5x output across the full request. Batch costs 50% of Standard; Fast costs 2x; Ultrafast costs 3 times the Standard rate through February 28, 2027, and 6 times the Standard rate starting March 1, 2027 (Pacific time). Launch benchmarks are OpenAI-reported; effort variants are recorded with each score.

benchmarks.name: Internal Research Debugging Evaluation
benchmarks.description: The Internal Research Debugging Evaluation measures whether models can debug 41 real bugs from internal OpenAI research experiments (plus alignment-auditing tasks), where the original solutions took experienced researchers hours to days. Passing corresponds to providing assistance that would unblock the user, including partial root-cause explanations or fixes.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Internal Research Debugging Evaluation, mean rubric score 74.66%. GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol system card, Table 5 (Research engineering and model-training results).

benchmarks.name: Ramp SWE-Bench v2
benchmarks.description: Ramp SWE-Bench v2 is Ramp Labs' private coding benchmark of 500 backend engineering tasks built from pull requests that Ramp's in-house coding agent merged into production after engineer review, across work shipped by more than 200 Ramp engineers. Each model gets a one-shot prompt in the same sandboxed copy of Ramp's codebase and must produce a review-ready patch. A panel of LLM judges compares the candidate patch with the engineer-reviewed merged solution; a task passes when there is no material difference where the merged solution is better. Scores are pass@1 at high reasoning effort with web tools disabled, with each model running in its lab's native agent harness (Ramp's v2.1 Native view).
benchmarks.analysis_method: pass@1 on 500 private Ramp production tasks (367/500 resolved, 95% CI +/-3.9 points), graded by Ramp's LLM judge panel against the merged patch. Codex harness, high reasoning effort, web tools disabled (Ramp SWE-Bench v2.1 Native view, run as gpt-6.2-sol-high).
benchmarks.verification_notes: Third-party evaluation by Ramp Labs; tasks are private and not reproduced by LLM Stats.

benchmarks.name: Ramp SWE-Bench v2 (Bash)
benchmarks.description: Ramp SWE-Bench v2 is Ramp Labs' private coding benchmark of 500 backend engineering tasks built from pull requests that Ramp's in-house coding agent merged into production after engineer review, across work shipped by more than 200 Ramp engineers. Each model gets a one-shot prompt in the same sandboxed copy of Ramp's codebase and must produce a review-ready patch. A panel of LLM judges compares the candidate patch with the engineer-reviewed merged solution; a task passes when there is no material difference where the merged solution is better. Scores are pass@1 at high reasoning effort with web tools disabled, with every model running in the same bash-only mini-swe-agent harness (Ramp's v2.0 Bash view), which isolates the model from harness differences.
benchmarks.analysis_method: pass@1 on 500 private Ramp production tasks (362/500 resolved, 95% CI +/-3.9 points), graded by Ramp's LLM judge panel against the merged patch. mini-swe-agent bash-only harness shared by every model, high reasoning effort, web tools disabled (Ramp SWE-Bench v2.0 Bash view, run as gpt-6.2-sol-high).
benchmarks.verification_notes: Third-party evaluation by Ramp Labs; tasks are private and not reproduced by LLM Stats.

benchmarks.name: SEC-bench Pro
benchmarks.description: SEC-bench Pro is a self-evolving software-security benchmark that measures agent bug hunting on critical, high-complexity systems. It instantiates validated vulnerabilities across the V8 and SpiderMonkey JavaScript engines as reproducible vulnerability-discovery and proof-of-concept-generation tasks with oracle-based validation.
benchmarks.analysis_method: SEC-Bench Pro, vulnerability reproduction (pass@1) 88.34%. GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol system card, Table 4 (Critical cybersecurity capability evaluations).
